title: Cedargrove Bank - Dedicated Capacity Discovery
summary: Discovery focused on dedicated GPU reservation, isolation/VPC needs, burst strategy and scaling SLAs. Customer interested in private control plane later; requested security docs and a benchmark run. Agreed next steps: send pricing, schedule technical deep dive and share SOC2/KMS notes.
action_items: Ryan Chen: Send Dedicated pricing deck and capacity options by 2026-12-03
Priya Kapoor: Schedule technical deep dive and benchmark run week of 2026-12-07
Tom Reyes: Share current infra topology and expected QPS by 2026-12-04
next_steps: Share SOC2 and private deployment docs
Provision short burst test window for benchmark
transcript:
[00:00] Ryan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Ryan at Redwood, with Priya from our SE team. How's it going?
[00:22] Mark (Cedargrove - CTO): Morning, morning. We got a short agenda, want to understand dedicated options — reserved GPUs, isolation, and how bursting works.
[00:45] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, thanks Mark. Quick intro on our side: Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with configurable autoscale and optional private control plane. We'll cover throughput/latency tradeoffs and burst.
[01:10] Aisha (Cedargrove - Head of ML): Quick context: we're moving from a small hosted POC on open models to heavier inference for our fraud detection flows, need deterministic latency and data isolation.
[01:35] Tom (Cedargrove - Infra): And we have strict network controls; anything that needs VPC peering or private endpoints is a must. Also KMS integration for keys.
[02:00] Ryan: Totally — those are common. Could you share target QPS and p99 latency goals? Even ballparks help.
[02:20] Mark: For the fraud scorer, peak about 600 qps across models, avg 240 qps. P99 we want under 120ms for short prompts, and under 300ms for large context.
[02:45] Priya: Ok that helps. Are these synchronous requests in-path of customer traffic? Any tolerance for async?
[03:05] Aisha: Yes, this is inline, so latency matters. We can accept small percent tail over 300ms but goal is under 150ms typically.
[03:30] Speaker 1: there's also the question of data retention — do we store prompts? we don't want logs kept beyond audit retention.
[03:50] Ryan: Redwood Dedicated supports customer isolation and can be deployed with a private control plane; logs/audit retention can be configured and we support KMS + HSM options for keys. We'll share SOC2 docs.
[04:15] Tom: Important: we need SSO (SAML) and RBAC controls for access to model endpoints and telemetry.
[04:35] Priya: We have SSO and fine-grained RBAC; for dedicated customers we map roles to org groups and can restrict access to model routes.
[04:55] Mark: Walk me through the reserved GPU model — we buy N GPUs, run a pool, how does bursting to cloud or shared capacity work?
[05:20] Priya: Good q. Reserved capacity is a pool of instances you commit to; autoscaling policies allow short-term burst above reserved capacity using burst buffer or on-demand shared capacity. We have policies for max burst percent and cost controls. In practice, typical pattern: reserve baseline for 90th perc, allow 2x burst for short windows.
[05:50] Aisha: So like if we reserve for 300 qps and spike to 600, Redwood can burst? How do you guarantee fallbacks if burst not available?
[06:10] Priya: If burst is unavailable, automatic fallback routes to compatible lower-capacity model variants or to a hosted fallback with throttling. We can also do graceful degradation: shorter context, quantized models for tails.
[06:35] Tom: That fallback sounds risky for us — can we keep everything on private capacity only?
[06:50] Ryan: Yes, for security- focused customers you can opt for private-only capacity; that requires planning for peak and slightly higher cost, but removes cross-tenant fallbacks.
[07:15] Mark: What's the procurement/contract cadence? Min commit?
[07:30] Ryan: Typical minimum is monthly reserved commit on a set of GPU types, annual contracts for discount. We can model different sizing scenarios in the deck.
[07:50] Speaker 2: i'm wondering about burst billing — is it pay-as-you-go for the burst portion?
[08:05] Ryan: Burst is billed at on-demand rates; we show line-items for reserved vs burst in pricing. You can cap burst spend.
[08:25] Aisha: Performance — can you run our specific model stack? We use a custom LLM fine-tuned internally and want to host it.
[08:45] Priya: We support customer model onboarding; we do kernel selection and can run quantized variants. We'll need a model binary or container; can you share model size and whether it uses KV caching heavily?
[09:05] Aisha: Model is 30B in FP16, uses KV cache for long contexts.
[09:20] Priya: 30B with KV cache is realistic on dedicated. We'll likely recommend multi-GPU sharding and a quantization profile for cost. That will affect latency; we'll include suggestions in the benchmark.
[09:45] Tom: Network egress/residency — we need all traffic to stay in our VPC and logs in our storage. Can we do private control plane in our VPC?
[10:05] Ryan: Yes, Redwood Private offers a private control plane option — can be VPC-deployed or on-prem. For Dedicated we can pair a private control plane so all admin/control plane traffic stays in your network.
[10:25] Mark: Timeframe — we're looking to be live in Q1 2027. Pilot first, then ramp.
[10:40] Ryan: That seems feasible. Pilot can be a small reserved pool with a week of benchmark testing.
[11:00] Aisha: On benchmarking — can Redwood run our synthetic load and measure p50/p95/p99 across payload sizes?
[11:20] Priya: Yep, SE-led benchmark. We typically run multiple profiles: short prompts, medium, large with KV cache warming and cold start scenarios.
[11:40] Mark: Cold start behavior is important, and how KV cache warmup affects tail latency.
[12:00] Priya: We'll instrument KV cache warmup and show warm vs cold numbers. Also show batching effects.
[12:20] Tom: Security audit — we need audit logs forwarded to our SIEM and proof of SOC2/ISO. Also KMS integration to bring-your-own-keys.
[12:45] Ryan: We'll share our SOC2 report and KMS integration guide. For dedicated/private deployments we support BYOK via KMS and HSM integrations.
[13:05] Speaker 3: what's the upgrade path if we outgrow the initial pool?
[13:20] Priya: You can scale up by adding more reserved nodes or change instance types. Online capacity changes require some orchestration but can be automated via our console and APIs.
[13:40] Aisha: Any recommendations on optimal reserved sizing strategy given our traffic distribution?
[13:55] Priya: We usually suggest reserving for 75–90th percentile steady-state and rely on controlled burst for known spikes. For strict SLA environments, reserve closer to 95th. We'll model cost curves.
[14:20] Mark: Can Redwood provide observability hooks — per-route latency, token-level cost, traces?
[14:40] Ryan: Yes, Redwood Console includes per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, traces, and error analysis. You can ingest traces into external systems too.
[15:00] Tom: Integration points — do you support Istio/Envoy sidecar patterns or only direct endpoints?
[15:20] Priya: We support standard REST/SDK endpoints; for private deployments you can front with your sidecar/proxy. We have recommended patterns for Envoy.
[15:40] Aisha: About model variants for fallback — how do you validate quality when falling back to quantized or smaller models?
[16:00] Priya: We tie regressions to eval suites and can do canary rollouts with automatic rollback if metrics deviate. We'll help set up prompt sets to validate.
[16:25] Mark: Cost — can you give a ballpark per-token cost delta between hosting on Dedicated vs Hosted for our model?
[16:45] Ryan: Roughly, dedicated amortized costs are lower at higher volume but come with reserved commit. Hosted is higher per-token but flexible. We'll include modeled examples based on your QPS and token lengths.
[17:10] Speaker 1: are there known partners for on-prem hardware or procurement?
[17:25] Ryan: We have partners and preferred configs we can share. For Private on-prem we also help with packaging.
[17:45] Tom: For the pilot, we want a short burst window where we can spike to 3x to test degradations. Can we get that?
[18:05] Priya: Yes, we can provision a burst window and coordinate a benchmark schedule.
[18:25] Aisha: Also want the ability to pin model versions and config for rollouts.
[18:40] Priya: Rollouts and pinning are supported — you can pin versions to a route and do canary percentages.
[19:00] Mark: Compliance question — data residency in EU for some users, we need region pinning.
[19:20] Ryan: Region pinning supported for Dedicated and Private; we'll note data residency options in the docs.
[19:40] Speaker 2: any limits on concurrency per connection?
[20:00] Priya: Limits configurable; default rate limits exist but can be adjusted for dedicated pools.
[20:20] Tom: For observability retention we may need 13 months of logs — is that an add-on?
[20:40] Ryan: That's an add-on; we offer extended observability retention and long-term storage integrations.
[21:00] Aisha: One thing — we use some internal routing logic that dials out to model endpoints, need guaranteed throughput per route.
[21:20] Priya: We can do per-route QoS and priority routing to ensure critical routes have reserved throughput.
[21:40] Mark: Let's talk rough timeline: pricing + sizing by Friday, then SE deep dive next week, benchmark during pilot week.
[22:00] Ryan: Sounds good. We'll send the pricing deck and a proposed pilot plan.
[22:20] Tom: Onboarding docs and infra checklist would be helpful.
[22:35] Ryan: We'll include an infra checklist and a short runbook.
[22:50] Aisha: Anything we should be aware of re: model licensing or export controls?
[23:10] Priya: We'll surface any model-specific licensing concerns during onboarding. If it's customer-owned model, licensing typically stays with you.
[23:30] Speaker 1: small note, sometimes the transcription misses specific acronyms, so we'll check the notes.
[23:45] Ryan: Great. Any other questions?
[24:00] Mark: No, that's it for now.
[24:10] Ryan: Recap: Ryan to send pricing & sizing, Priya to schedule deep dive and benchmarks, Tom to share infra details. We'll also share SOC2 and KMS docs.
[24:35] Aisha: Good. Also please include example cost curves and reserve vs burst scenarios.
[24:50] Ryan: Will do. Thanks all.
[25:00] Priya: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invites.
[25:10] Mark: Thanks everyone.
[25:20] END_TRANSCRIPT
